title: Stock Market Today Live: Markets shed morning gains; Sensex up 113 pts, Nifty trades below 24,000 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 3 September 2026

At 1:20 pm, Sensex was up 113.05 pts or 0.15% higher at 76,683.40. Nifty was up 17.50 pts or 0.073% at 23,931.95.

The Sensex was trading at 76,593.78, up just 23.43 points or 0.03 per cent, while the Nifty 50 was at 23,913.20, down 1.25 points or 0.01 per cent, as of 12.45 PM, a sharp pullback from the positive open that had taken the Nifty close to the 24,000 mark. On the BSE, 2,436 stocks were advancing against 1,673 declining, with 234 unchanged. A total of 155 stocks hit 52-week highs while 82 touched 52-week lows.

Banking stocks remained the standout performers. Adani Ports was the top Nifty gainer, up 1.85 per cent to ₹1,703.70. Axis Bank rose 1.55 per cent to ₹1,273.30, ICICI Bank gained 1.04 per cent to ₹1,441.30, SBI advanced 0.84 per cent to ₹1,029.50, and HDFC Bank added 0.84 per cent to ₹706.70. Realty stocks also gained over 2 per cent in early trade, though the broader market failed to sustain the momentum.

On the losing side, Titan fell 2.12 per cent to ₹4,966.50 from a previous close of ₹5,074.00. Cipla dropped 1.41 per cent to ₹1,392.90, extending pressure on the pharma sector. Tech Mahindra declined 1.18 per cent to ₹1,603.90, continuing Wednesday’s weakness in IT. Eicher Motors fell 1.16 per cent to ₹7,622.00, reflecting continued stress in the auto segment, while Nestle India slipped 1.09 per cent to ₹1,409.50, weighing on the FMCG space.

Infosys Ltd informed that step-down wholly-owned subsidiaries of the company have been voluntarily liquidated:

1. Guidevision UK Ltd has been voluntarily liquidated effective September 1, 2026.

2. In-tech Automotive Engineering Beijing Co., Ltd (“in-tech (Beijing) Information Technology Co. Ltd”), has been voluntarily liquidated, effective September 2, 2026

smallcase has announced the launch of US Equities smallcases, enabling Indian investors to invest in professionally curated portfolios of US-listed stocks and global ETFs. Building on the launch of direct US equities earlier this year, the offering expands smallcase’s global investing ecosystem by bringing its model portfolio investing experience to international markets.

US Equity smallcases allow investors to discover and invest in professionally managed portfolios built around long-term investment strategies, sectors and themes. With fractional investing enabled, the smallcase app makes global diversification more accessible by allowing investors to invest in companies without having to purchase whole shares, with global strategies available from just $50.

The offering is powered by smallcase’s end-to-end portfolio investing infrastructure and leverages the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) Global Access Provider (GAP) framework. Investments are facilitated through an IFSCA-registered Global Access Provider at GIFT City for US broking services and an IFSCA-registered payment service provider for seamless fund transfers under the Reserve Bank of India’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS).

Bank of India has decided to exercise the call option on Bank of India Tier II Bonds Series XV (ISIN No. INE084A08151) and declare Tuesday, 15 September 2026 as the record date for this purpose. The bonds were issued on 30 September 2021 in pursuance of terms mentioned in the Information Memorandum dated 29 September 2021. The bonds carry a coupon rate of 7.14% per annum, payable annually, with a call option on 30 September 2026. The bank will pay broken period interest and the call option amount (principal) on 30 September 2026.

GCPL shares hit a 52-week low as new CEO's inventory correction plan raises investor concerns, leading to a 4% decline.

Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty trim gains as banking stocks rise while IT, Pharma, and Consumer sectors weigh down performance.

Autoline Industries has secured a new business award from Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd for the supply of critical components for SUV applications.

Top gainers of the Nifty Midcap 100: BSE (+4.42%), SBI Cards (+3.45%), Blue Star (+3.35%) and KEI Industries (+2.96%). Top losers: MCX (-3.12%), APL Apollo (-2.76%), Bharat Forge (-2.30%), Federal Bank (-2.09%) and 360 ONE WAM (-1.83%).

Markets were off the day’s high. The Sensex was up 46.32 points, or 0.06%, to 76,616.67, and the Nifty 50 slipped 2.25 points, or 0.01%, to 23,912.20.

Balkrishna Industries Ltd has approved the issue of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) aggregating to ₹550 crore.

XTGlobal has been selected for a multi-year US state government cloud engineering, AI/ML and generative AI programme.

Canara Bank has approved the raising of foreign currency funds through the issuance of senior unsecured foreign currency bonds (fixed rated / floating rated) of up to $2,000 million in the international market under the existing $3 billion Medium Term Note (MTN) Programme, through the IBU GIFT City branch, Gandhinagar, or any other overseas branch. Shares were up 1% to ₹127.63 on the NSE.

Options turnover fell 20% in August, the first month of the new mechanism, while algorithmic traders say they have sharply reduced activity amid volatile closing prices.

Anant Raj shares surge 8% in midday trade, becoming top Nifty Realty gainer amid heavy volume and positive corporate developments.
